cause: The diagnostic used Counter.update(record), so JSON values were interpreted as counts.
impact: Read-only diagnostic stopped; no dataset or result was modified.
recovery: Reran the inventory with Counter.update(record.keys()) and used the corrected output.

cause: Windows sandbox denied process creation with the worktree as the child working directory.
impact: No command body ran and no file was modified.
recovery: Ran subsequent commands from the repository root with the worktree path explicit.

cause: The diagnostic guessed semgrep-rules.yaml and bandit-findings.json instead of resolving names from policy.lock.json.
impact: Two read operations failed; the Oracle material was not missing or changed.
recovery: Resolved and read semgrep.yml, bandit.yml, and bandit-metadata.json through the lock file.

cause: A foreach statement result was piped without first assigning it to a variable.
impact: The read-only hash check did not execute and no artifact changed.
recovery: Collected the loop output in a variable and reran the check.

cause: The first scope-decision draft contained non-authoritative prompt hashes.
impact: All four provenance comparisons failed before the audit command was run; no result directory was created.
recovery: Replaced all four hashes with the authoritative values from frozen functional-audit packets and retained validation as a hard gate.

cause: The fixed project virtual environment does not install the optional Ruff executable.
impact: The first format and lint invocation did not run; test results were unaffected.
recovery: Located the already cached Ruff 0.16.2 through uv and kept the check offline.

cause: The new command used legacy Typer default-call syntax and the module had two mechanical style findings.
impact: Ruff reported eight findings after formatting two files; no runtime result was treated as final.
recovery: Changed the command to Annotated option declarations, sorted imports, simplified the annotation, and scheduled a new immutable v2 audit after revalidation.

cause: A double-quoted PowerShell command expanded the intended remote shell variable before SSH execution.
impact: The first read attempted /summary.json and failed; the remote execution artifacts remained intact.
recovery: Reran the read with a single-quoted remote command and full absolute paths.
